title: Irisa Claude, Sorry I mean Irisa Prime
excerpt: My interview at Irisa Prime, a company that doesn't hire, doesn't need AI, and sits on a money hole called Foolad Mobarakeh.

blocks.text: Well well, we've come to the fascinating Irisa company and the Irisa Prime section, maybe better to say Irisa SubPrime...
This Irisa company is very famous in Isfahan, because the story is that in the city of Isfahan, you can only find a few useful companies that are worth working at...
Now where are they connected to? To the Foolad Mobarakeh Isfahan company - if you don't know where it is, to put it very briefly, a hole that produces unlimited money :)

Yeah... imagine a table where everyone is sitting in a corner and eating money. Basically Irisa is the same. Of course, is this bad? No! But on the condition that the work you do creates value. Well, good for you, you get paid for it. But when you're extra and shove apps and various useless things into an organization's pants so you get paid and don't starve, that's no longer called working :)
The Invitation

I was invited to this interview through one of my friends at the University of Isfahan. It was mostly for the RAG and LLM and chatbot development field. I had also done these things in my master's and I have a good familiarity with this field.

On the interview day I went and arrived 15 minutes early, good memory, I went from the university itself. I sat down at the bottom of the company and my phone signal died, I don't know, it's like it happened on purpose but well I really had no signal.
Then the question that comes up is, man, what important thing is happening that you have all this security phase? I'd appreciate if someone answers this question.
Anyway, a guy who was security and sat at the door and his job was basically hassling women's clothing and he gets paid for this said go up.
The Fifth Floor

I went to the 5th floor. Meanwhile, I have another friend who works at Irisa but in another section, and I informed him that I'm here and he said whenever your interview is done, message me so I see you.
Anyway, I went to the 5th floor and knocked and entered that section.
A bunch of people were behind computers and a few Claude accounts were also up and they were giving prompts :) Yeah, it was Prime 😂 maybe Irisa Claude isn't a bad title either...

A lady came, F.T.(F is her first name, not Fuck 😂), who was the head of that section, and said let's go up for the interview. I don't know which floor we went to but it was so high that the roof was above our heads. We went into a hall where they didn't know how to turn on its light and two people were simultaneously struggling to turn on the lamps.
It was a meeting room and they completely couldn't turn on the lights. Irisa had become an escape room.
The Interview Questions
They started asking: explain a complete RAG pipeline. We want to build a question and answer pet bot. And my answer was: it depends.
Because it really does depend, the choice of technologies and approaches must match the data we're working with. Is it image? Text? Audio? What is it, man?
Basically they also told me don't say it depends - explain! Then when I asked about different cases they didn't give me a correct answer.

My thought here was that, well, for example, choosing a VECTOR DB for a chatbot is very different if it has 100 users or 2 million! I mean, I had worked at Snapp Carfix - a place where we had 1.5 million users and I had a correct understanding of system scale.
And suddenly he turned and said imagine we have 300 users :) and I was like, man, this is a happy game!
Whatever!

They asked various questions from my resume. He asked about Lakehouse or for example a course project where I had worked with MinIO and such, and well it was for a year ago and I really didn't remember the details of the projects and I honestly said I don't remember.

He said if instead of AI we want you to work on database and Lakehouse and such, is it okay? I said no :) He said you don't like it or is your answer just no? I said well I like to work in line with my expertise. These have nothing to do with me.

Another lady who was there also asked about my papers, where I submitted them, and I answered her and she said: what is your goal in general? Do you like to stay in academic fields or do you like to work with industry?
I also said I feel much better in academic work.
Then she said where do you see your future? I also said, honestly, when I sleep tonight I don't know if a missile will hit our house or not.. what future?
When we reached the end of the interview they said we don't have hiring 😂 crazy dumbass, well why do you interview?

I also said okay and I really didn't give a shit. Of course I think these jobless people didn't even think that someone would not care about them like this, because their name is big but the result of their work is like the main theme of my website, Glassy 😂
In the end I messaged my friend and went and saw him and we talked and laughed and I went hoooome :)
A Few Last Words
1: In my opinion, 90% of Iranian businesses have no need for AI.

When Iranian companies and big corporations are sanctioned and have no connection with the world, they practically work in a closed environment and this closed environment brings erosion and they really don't have any particular progress. They step in place and stay alive.
2: Irisa company has many different sections, my experience is only about this  Irisa Prime section, not other sections.
3: Have honor. When you work somewhere, don't sell extra and useless solutions and products into the company just to get money. Be realistic. You have no need for AI.

Most of your projects have failed and your Arash chatbot is practically equal to Bard... What was Bard? Good memory, it was Gemini's grandfather. It was so shitty that Google deleted it from the foundation.

4: The outputs of this section practically have no efficiency and through the communications I had with the employees and end users of these companies, they all said that this project was never operational and failed.

5: In my opinion, the Loosers who work in these sections better go and really work! Work that brings value. Not that they shove something under attractive titles like smartization and AI and such into companies' pants and in the end it has no added value.

6: When you sit in front of someone as an interviewer, it's natural that your understanding and experience in the field you work in at your company is higher than that person, so don't instill the feeling that you are superior and that person doesn't know anything. Give people a chance, respect so you get respect.
Is Irisa Prime a Good Place to Work?
In my opinion it depends on yourself. If you like to now have an AI title in your resume and in practice be unemployed and sit at a table where you get money, yeah it's good.
But if you want to work in an environment where the result of your efforts is really seen and you are value-creating, don't be fooled by its name. It's really not worth it.
And the last question: name one Irisa Cluade product that is on Production and successful - 100 points.
Irisa Claude
